name: Aaron
description: Aaron, brother of Moses and first high priest of Israel.

name: Abel
description: Abel, the just son of Adam whose innocent blood was shed by his brother Cain.

name: Adam
description: Adam, the first man, whose creation and fall prefigure Christ as the New Adam.

name: Ahithophel
description: Achitophel, David's trusted counselor who betrayed him; a figure of the perfidious Judas (Ps 40:10, 'lifted up his heel').

name: Anointing of Kings, Priests, and Prophets
Antiochus Epiphanes
description: The Hellenistic king and great persecutor of God's people (the 'little horn'); a figure of Antichrist.

name: Babylon
description: The ancient city of Babylon, the city of confusion, idolatry, and oppression of God's people.

name: Balaam
description: Balaam, the pagan seer whose oracles included the prophecy of the Star from Jacob (Numbers 24:17).

name: Binding of Isaac
description: Abraham's willing sacrifice of his son Isaac on Mount Moriah (Genesis 22).

name: Brazen Serpent
description: The bronze serpent Moses lifted up on a pole in the wilderness so that all who looked upon it were healed (Numbers 21:8-9).

name: Burning Bush
description: The bush that burned with fire but was not consumed, in which the Angel of the Lord appeared to Moses (Exodus 3).

name: Ceremonial Law
description: The ceremonial and ritual prescriptions of the Old Testament Law, fulfilled and surpassed in the New Covenant.

name: Circumcision
description: The sign of the covenant given to Abraham, marking incorporation into the people of God.

name: Cloud in the Desert
description: The pillar of cloud that guided and protected Israel through the wilderness.

name: Crossing of the Jordan
description: Israel's passage through the Jordan River into the Promised Land under Joshua.

name: Crossing of the Red Sea
description: Israel's passage through the Red Sea, liberated from Egyptian slavery and passing dry-shod through the waters.

name: Cyrus
description: Cyrus the Persian, who overthrew Babylon and freed the captives; a figure of the Messiah, the executor of divine justice (Isa 41:2; 45:1).

name: Daniel's Four Beasts (Four Empires)
description: The four beasts of Daniel 7 (lion/Chaldean, bear/Persian, leopard/Greek, and the fourth/Roman empire); the composite beast of Revelation alludes to them, figuring the final apostate empire of Antichrist.

name: Dietary Laws
description: The Mosaic laws distinguishing clean and unclean animals (Leviticus 11, Deuteronomy 14).

name: Divine Fire (Lightning)
description: The fire/lightning of God's power in Ps 28(29); a figure of the Holy Spirit appearing as tongues of fire at Pentecost.

name: Edom
description: Edom and Bosra, conquered enemies; taken mystically for the enemies of Christ and his Church.

name: Esau
description: Esau, who lost his birthright and privileges to Jacob; a figure of the reprobate, though not himself necessarily reprobate.

name: Esther
description: Queen Esther, who interceded for her people and secured their deliverance; a figure of the Church and of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

name: Eve
description: Eve, the first woman and mother of all the living.

name: Feast of Pentecost
description: The Feast of Weeks (Shavuot), celebrating the firstfruits of the harvest and the giving of the Law at Sinai.

name: Gideon
description: Gideon, judge of Israel who delivered his people with a small band chosen by God.

name: God's Deliverance from Sennacherib
description: God's overthrow of Sennacherib's army, terrifying the persecutors; a figure of the certainty of the final judgment.

name: God's Healing Word
description: God's word/command by which the sick were healed; read by the Fathers in the prophetical sense of Christ the Word who heals.

name: God's Wonders by Water
description: The many wonders God wrought by water in the Old Testament (Exodus plagues, provision in the wilderness); a figure of the grace conferred in baptism.

name: Gog and Magog
description: Gog and Magog of Ezekiel's prophecy — nations gathered against God's people; a figure of the last persecution of the Church under Antichrist before the final judgment.

name: Hezekiah
description: King Ezechias of Judah, righteous king delivered from the Assyrians; figure of Christ and of the Church persecuted yet increasing.

name: Holofernes
description: The pagan general in Judith who demands universal worship and divine status; a figure of Antichrist.

name: Hosea
description: The prophet Osee, who took back the unfaithful woman; acting 'as a figure of the Lord, who has received an outrage' yet offers grace to penitent sinners.

name: Isaac
description: Isaac, son of the free-woman Sarah and child of promise; in Paul's allegory (Gal 4) a figure of the New Covenant, the free children of God, and the Church.

name: Isaiah (the prophet)
description: The prophet Isaiah, anointed by God's Spirit to preach good news to the poor; a figure of Christ the Anointed One (Luke 4:18).

name: Ishmael
description: Ishmael, son of Abraham by Hagar, the son of the bondwoman born according to the flesh.

name: Israel (Jeshurun)
description: Israel under the title Jeshurun, the beloved of God; a figure of the Messiah, the true Beloved.

name: Israel's Disobedience in the Wilderness
description: The murmurs, infidelities, and disobedience of the Hebrews in the desert; written 'in a figure' (1 Cor 10:6) as a warning that the sacraments without amendment bring condemnation.

name: Jacob
description: Jacob (Israel), patriarch whose life of struggle and sorrow prefigures Christ.

name: Jeremiah
description: The prophet Jeremiah, persecuted and afflicted; a figure of Christ in his sufferings.

name: Job
description: The innocent sufferer whose trials, vindication, and restoration figure Christ (the innocent man of sorrows), the Church, and the resurrection of the just.

name: Jonah
description: The prophet Jonah, three days in the belly of the fish; a figure of Christ's resurrection (the sign of Jonas, Matt 12:40).

name: Josedec
description: Jesus son of Josedech, high priest who returned from exile and helped rebuild the temple (Hag, Zech); a figure of Christ the High Priest and builder of the spiritual temple.

name: Joseph
description: Joseph, son of Jacob, sold by his brothers yet exalted to deliver his people from famine.

name: Joshua
description: Joshua (Yehoshua), successor of Moses who led Israel into the Promised Land.

name: Judah
description: Judah, son of Jacob, from whose tribe the Messiah descends (Genesis 49).

name: Judas Maccabeus
description: The Maccabean warrior who conquered Idumea and fought to save his people; a glorious figure of Christ the victorious conqueror (read of the ascension).

name: Judith
description: The widow of Israel who delivered her people by slaying Holofernes; a figure of the Blessed Virgin Mary and of the Church.

name: Leah
description: Leah, first wife of Jacob, mother of six of the twelve tribes.

name: Leviathan
description: The great sea-monster of Job, fearsome yet subject to God; represents the devil under God's dominion.

name: Levitical Leprosy Laws
description: The Levitical laws governing the diagnosis, quarantine, and purification of leprosy (Leviticus 13-14).

name: Levitical Purifications (Ceremonial Washings)
description: The ceremonial purifications of the Old Law with water; figures of baptism and penance, in which the blood of Christ is applied to the soul.

name: Liver of the Fish (Tobit)
description: The fish's liver burned to expel the demon Asmodeus in Tobit; read mystically as the means of demonic deliverance.

name: Manna in the Desert
description: The bread from heaven that fed Israel during their forty years in the wilderness.

name: Melchizedek
description: The priest-king of Salem who offered bread and wine and blessed Abraham.

name: Miriam
description: Miriam, sister of Moses and Aaron, prophetess of Israel.

name: Moses
description: Moses, liberator and lawgiver of Israel, mediator of the Old Covenant.

name: Moses's Veil
description: The veil Moses placed over his face to hide the fading glory of the law (Exod 34); a figure of the obscurity and transience of the old covenant, removed in the unveiled glory of the new (2 Cor 3).

name: Nehemiah
description: Nehemiah, whose name means 'comforter of God,' sent by the king to rebuild Jerusalem; a figure of Christ sent to comfort and establish the Church.

name: Noah
description: Noah, the just man who found favor with God and was preserved through the Flood.

name: Noah's Ark
description: The ark built by Noah that preserved his family through the flood waters.

name: Noah's Flood
description: The flood that cleansed the earth in the days of Noah, through which eight persons were saved by water.

name: Old Testament Priesthood
description: The Levitical priesthood established at Sinai for sacrifice and mediation.

name: Old Testament Sacrifices
description: The various sacrifices and offerings prescribed in the Law of Moses.

name: Passover
description: The feast commemorating Israel's liberation from Egypt, including the paschal lamb and unleavened bread.

name: Proselytes (Strangers in Israel)
description: Foreign strangers/proselytes who renounced idolatry, embraced Israel's religion, and were incorporated into the covenant community.

name: Raphael
description: The angel Raphael in Tobit, who appears in human form to guide and protect Tobias; commentary reads him as prefiguring Christ's assumption of human nature.

name: Rebecca
description: Rebecca, wife of Isaac, chosen by divine providence as bride for the patriarch's son.

name: Red Heifer
description: The red heifer sacrifice prescribed in Numbers 19, whose ashes mixed with water purified those defiled by contact with the dead.

name: Return from Babylonian Captivity
description: The restored holy people returning from captivity to rebuilt Jerusalem, described by the prophets as a sanctified community; a figure of the Church.

name: Sanaballat
description: Sanballat, persecutor of the Jewish restoration and friend of Tobias; prefigures heretics who oppose the true faith.

name: Sarah
description: Sarah, wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac, the free woman whose son was born according to the promise.

name: Sennacherib
description: The Assyrian king who spoiled Samaria and Judah and despised God, then was brought to nothing; a figure of the persecutors of the Church.

name: Solomon
description: King Solomon, son of David, whose name means 'peaceable' and whose peaceful reign and temple-building prefigure Christ.

name: Temporal Chastisements of Israel
description: The temporal punishments inflicted on Israel for sin (e.g. the slaying of the murmurers, Num 25); types of eternal chastisement (1 Cor 10:11).

name: Temporal Rewards of the Old Law
description: The material blessings and temporal prosperity God granted the just under the Old Covenant, given as a figure of heavenly rewards.

name: The Abomination of Desolation
description: The profanation of the temple foretold by Daniel (partly fulfilled by Pilate's and Adrian's images), prefiguring the abomination Antichrist will bring at the end.

name: The Altar of Incense
description: The golden altar of incense in the holy place, where incense was offered morning and evening; signifies Christ the Mediator, through whose merits the prayers of the faithful ascend.

name: The Angel of the Lord
description: The angel who encamps round God's servants to guard them (Ps 33/34); read by the Fathers as figuring Christ the protector.

name: The Ark of the Covenant
description: The ark where God's presence dwelt, which David longed to be near; a figure of heaven, the place of God's presence.

name: The Ass and the Colt (Palm Sunday)
description: The ass and the colt of Zech 9:9, read by the Fathers as figuring the Jews (ass) and Gentiles (colt) to be loosed and brought to Christ, united in his Church.

name: The Babylonian Exile
description: Israel's exile, deprived of religion, temple, and princes; a figure of the long desolation the Jews endured after rejecting Christ.

name: The Cup of Divine Wrath
description: The cup/chalice of God's judgment in which the dregs are reserved for sinners; a figure of the eschatological cup of wrath at the last judgment.

name: The Divine Chariot Theophany
description: God appearing on his chariot of winds/clouds (cf. Ezek 1:4) to come to David's aid; read by the Fathers as figuring Christ's ascension.

name: The Dove and the Olive Branch (Noah)
description: The dove returning to the ark with an olive branch (Gen 8:11), signifying peace and deliverance from the flood; a figure of the peace conferred in baptism.

name: The Exodus from Egypt
description: God's deliverance of Israel from Egyptian bondage; a figure of the redemption of mankind by Christ.

name: The Faithful Remnant
description: The few of Israel preserved through judgment (e.g. under Hezekiah after the Assyrians); a figure of the remnant who embrace the faith of Christ (Rom 9:27).

name: The Feast on Mount Zion
description: Isaiah's prophesied banquet of rich food and wine on Mount Zion for all nations; a figure of the Eucharist and the heavenly banquet.

name: The Foolish Shepherd
description: The foolish/idol shepherd of Zech 11:15, representing the wicked princes and priests (and emperors like Caligula and Nero) who rule before the desolation of Jerusalem.

name: The Gates Lifted for the King of Glory
description: The eternal gates commanded to lift up their heads for the triumphal entry of the King of Glory (Ps 23/24); a figure of Christ's ascension into heaven.

name: The Glory of the Lord Departing the Temple
description: The divine glory on the throne departing Jerusalem by way of Mount Olivet (Ezek 11:23); read of Christ (two natures on the throne) ascending from Olivet.

name: The Heavenly Jerusalem (Prophetic Vision)
description: The OT prophetic vision of Jerusalem adorned with precious stones and gold (Tobit 13 / Isaiah 54), prefiguring the glorified Church.

name: The Heavens
description: The heavens and stars that silently declare God's glory; read as figuring the Church and her apostolic preachers.

name: The Holy of Holies
description: The innermost sanctuary of the tabernacle/temple, entered once a year by the high priest; a figure of heaven, into which Christ entered by his ascension (Heb 6; 9).

name: The Invitation to the Waters (Isaiah 55)
description: Isaiah's invitation to all who thirst to come to the waters, milk, and wine without price; a figure of Christ's invitation and the grace of the sacraments.

name: The King of Tyre
description: The king of Tyre, 'the seal of resemblance,' whose pride is commonly understood of Lucifer.

name: The Kings of Sheba Bearing Gifts
description: The kings of Sheba and Ephah prophesied to come bearing gold and frankincense (Isa 60:6); fulfilled in the Magi adoring Christ.

name: The Living Waters from the Sanctuary
description: The fountain of water flowing from Jerusalem/the temple (Joel 3:18; Ezek 47); a figure of the fountain of grace in the Church militant and of glory in the Church triumphant.

name: The Mark of Tau
description: The mark Tau (in ancient Hebrew the form of a cross) set on the foreheads of the righteous to spare them (Ezek 9:4); a figure of the sign of Christ's cross in baptism.

name: The Mincha (Unbloody Sacrifice)
description: The mincha, the unbloody grain/flour offering of the Old Law; a figure of the Mass.

name: The Mosaic Law
description: The Law (Torah) given to Israel; perfected and fulfilled by the Gospel of Christ (Matt 5:17).

name: The Pool of Siloam
description: The pool of Siloe ('sent') at Jerusalem; its waters figure the sacrament of baptism, and its name figures Christ the Sent One.

name: The Promised Land
description: The land of Israel/Judea where right worship was observed; a figure of heaven, 'the land of rectitude.'

name: The Prophets
description: The Old Testament prophets, who represented God under visible forms and prefigured Christ, the end of the law.

name: The Rebuilt Temple
description: The second temple, rebuilt under Persian patronage after the exile, enduring despite adversity; a figure of the Church's indestructibility.

name: The Rechabites
description: The Rechabites who kept strict ascetic rules and abstained from lawful things for greater perfection; a figure of the religious orders of the Church.

name: The Rejected Cornerstone
description: The stone the builders rejected, become the head of the corner (Ps 117:22); applied to David/Zorobabel/Israel as figures of Christ, rejected then made the foundation.

name: The Shepherd of Israel
description: God/the Messiah portrayed as a shepherd ruling, guiding, and feeding his flock (Ps 23; Ezek 34); fulfilled in Christ the Lamb-Shepherd who leads the saints to fountains of living water.

name: The Son of Isaiah (Emmanuel sign)
description: The child to be born of Isaiah (Isa 8:4) as a near-term sign of deliverance; a prefigurement of Christ the true Emmanuel.

name: The Spouse of the Canticle (Song of Songs)
description: The bride/spouse of the Song of Songs, read as the Church seeking and united to Christ the one true Shepherd-Bridegroom.

name: The Stone (Daniel's Vision)
description: The stone cut without hands that shattered the four kingdoms and became a mountain filling the earth (Dan 2); a figure of Christ's eternal kingdom, the Church.

name: The Sun
description: The sun set in the firmament, giving light and warmth to all the world; read as figuring Christ, the Sun of Justice.

name: The Synagogue (Old Covenant Assembly)
description: The synagogue/assembly of the Old Covenant which rejected the Messiah; contrasted with the Church that received him as head.

name: The Table of Showbread (Bread of the Presence)
The Temple of Jerusalem
description: The material temple/sanctuary on Zion, stable and singular; fulfilled in the Church and figuring the heavenly dwelling.

name: The Threshing Floor
description: The threshing floor where grain is separated from chaff by winnowing; a figure of the Church, where the elect are distinguished from the reprobate.

name: The Twelve Patriarchs
description: The twelve patriarchs, ancestral heads of the tribes of Israel; prefiguring the twelve apostles.

name: The Unbroken Bones of the Just
description: The bones of the just man that shall not be broken (Ps 33/34:21); fulfilled in Christ, whose bones were not broken (John 19:36).

name: The Virgin of Emmanuel (Isaiah 7:14)
description: The virgin (almah) who shall conceive and bear Emmanuel; fulfilled in the Virgin Mary's conception of Christ.

name: The Voice of the Lord (Thunder)
description: The sevenfold 'voice of the Lord' (thunder) in Ps 28(29); read of Christ's powerful preaching, his baptism, and the sacraments.

name: The Year of Jubilee
description: The Jubilee year (Lev 25) of liberation, debt-forgiveness, and restoration; a figure of Christ's redemption.

name: Water from the Rock
description: Water that flowed from the rock struck by Moses at Horeb/Meribah to quench Israel's thirst.

name: Wilderness Pilgrimage toward the Promised Land
description: Israel's forty-year journey through the wilderness toward the earthly Promised Land.

name: Zechariah's Thirty Pieces of Silver
description: The prophet's symbolic action of receiving thirty pieces of silver (the 'handsome price,' ironically) and casting them to the potter in the house of the Lord (Zech 11:12-13); fulfilled in Judas's betrayal.

name: Zedekiah
description: Sedecias, the last king of Judah, rejected and afflicted; read as figuring Christ rejected and treated thus for the sins of mankind.

name: Zorobabel
description: The post-exilic leader who, though highly regarded, never truly possessed the throne; a figure of Christ, lest the Jews think the prophecies fulfilled in him.

name: Babylon the Great (the Harlot)
description: The mystical Babylon of Revelation — Rome and all wicked great cities / the multitude of the wicked who persecute the faithful — destined for judgment.

name: Baptism
description: The sacrament of regeneration and incorporation into Christ through water and the Spirit.

name: Christ
description: Jesus Christ, the incarnate Son of God and fulfillment of all Old Testament types.

name: Christ the High Priest
description: Christ as the eternal high priest who offered himself once for all on the cross.

name: Christ's Ascension
description: Christ's ascension into heaven and exaltation to the right hand of the Father.

name: Christ's Passion
description: The suffering and crucifixion of Jesus Christ for the redemption of mankind.

name: Christ's Victory
description: Christ's triumph over sin, death, and Satan through the Paschal Mystery.

name: Descent of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost
Destruction of Jerusalem as Divine Judgment
Eternal Life
description: The blessed inheritance of heaven promised to those who are baptized into Christ.

name: Eucharist
description: The sacrament of Christ's Body and Blood under the appearances of bread and wine.

name: Final Judgment
description: The Last Judgment at the end of time, when Christ will judge the living and the dead.

name: Heaven
description: The heavenly tabernacle and city, the eternal dwelling place of God and his people (Apoc 15:5; Heb 12:22).

name: Heretics
description: Those who teach false doctrine and oppose the true faith within the Christian era.

name: Holy Orders
description: The Sacrament of Holy Orders, by which men are ordained to the Christian priesthood.

name: John the Baptist
description: John the Baptist, who came in the spirit and power of Elijah to prepare the way before Christ's first coming (Matt 11:14; 17:11).

name: Mary
description: The Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of God and Mother of the Church.

name: Persecutors of the Church
description: Those who persecute the Christian Church and, like their OT figures, are ultimately judged.

name: Religious Orders (Consecrated Life)
description: The consecrated religious orders of the Church, professing poverty, chastity, and obedience in imitation of the apostles (Matt 19:12).

name: Sacraments of the New Covenant
description: The seven sacraments instituted by Christ as signs and means of grace.

name: Satan (the Devil)
description: The spiritual adversary who, despite his power, is ultimately subject to God and defeated by Christ.

name: Spiritual Gifts of Christ
description: The grace and spiritual refreshment that flows from Christ to believers.

name: The Adoration of the Magi
description: The wise men from the East who came to adore the infant Christ with gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh (Matt 2).

name: The Betrayal by Judas
description: Judas, who ate bread with Christ and was entrusted with the purse, betraying him with a kiss (John 13:18).

name: The Conversion of the Jews
description: The final conversion and restoration of the Jewish people, by which 'all Israel shall be saved' (Rom 11:26).

name: The Elect (Predestinate)
description: Those whom God has chosen and predestined to eternal glory by his mercy, apart from any foreseen merits.

name: The Gentiles Grafted into Christ's Church
The Gospel (New Covenant)
description: The Gospel of Jesus Christ, the New Covenant which fulfills and perfects the Law.

name: The Holy Spirit as Divine Guide
description: The Holy Spirit who guides the Church and individual believers, as the pillar of cloud guided Israel.

name: The Reprobate (the Rejected)
description: Those rejected by God and excluded from salvation, in contrast to the elect.

name: The Resurrection
description: The resurrection of Christ and the consequent bodily resurrection of believers.

name: The Synagogue as Preparation for the Church
The Synagogue's Persecution of the Church
The Twelve Apostles
description: The twelve apostles chosen by Christ, from whom the Christian people descend according to the spirit.
